harp-rocking.hears: The lullaby's rocking: the harp and violas' four-note cell (Bb-Ab-Bb-Cb, later Bb-Cb-C-Cb), one soft note every ~1.1 s from 6.6 to 172 s, slowing to 2-8 s apart at the very end (174-191 s). Measured in the audio (strongest pitch of Ab3-C4); none in the strings' swell 80-110 s.

berceuse-harp-track.hears: The piano track in the Berceuse, which is the harp (and celesta): the first Eb-Bb chord and cell (6.6-14.3 s), single high touches (31, 60-66 s), the bell-like F#5/F#6 harmonics of the bridge (110-115 s), the low Eb chords at the fade (164-175 s) and the last B3/B4 (191.4 s).

eb-pedal.hears: The Berceuse's floor: the low Eb2/Bb2 of cellos and harp (below MIDI 50), held 1-5 s each, from 6.6 to 175 s, plus the tremolo Eb2 at 180 s (merged into one note). Few and soft (v 27-63): a toll every few seconds where the transcriber heard it.

lullaby-bassoon.hears: The bassoon lullaby (Eb minor): the wind-labelled notes (bassoon, clarinet, horn, voice tracks: the transcriber splits the one bassoon among them) of its two phrases, 18.85-31.3 s (Eb4-Bb3-D4-Bb3-Eb4 ...) and 46.5-56 s. Soft (v 24-53), 0.3-1.6 s notes; the stretch 31-46 s between them is untranscribed.

wind-answers.hears: The woodwinds' soft chordal answers (two or more wind-labelled notes at once): 21.7-29.8 s, 49.9-59.0 s, single ones at 106.9 and 129.5 s, then the reprise's wind choir 139.7-153.5 s (Eb4/E4/F4 with E5-F5-Bb5 above). The answering voice to the bassoon.

voice-track.hears: Everything on YourMT3+'s "voice" track (19 notes; there is no singer: in the Berceuse these are the oboe-like answers B4-Bb4 at 39.5, 67.8-68.9, 76.9, 162.2-162.7 s, in the Finale a few inner notes at 280-282 and 336-342 s). Honest label: listen "voice" gives the same notes.

strings-lament.hears: Before the swell: the violins take the line, Ab4-C5-B4-Eb5 ... F#4 (3 s) ... E4 (3.2 s), 60.5-79.9 s: slow, soft (v 27-50), sighing down.

swell-violins.hears: The Berceuse's one swell (79.9-110 s, the loudest of the first movement, -16 dB at 88 s): the violins' long notes Ab5 (5.7 s), G5-F#5-Ab5-G5, D5 (5.6 s), then over the D pedal E5, Ab5, G5-F#5-Ab5-G5-F#5-F5. Held, aching, v 58-82.

swell-entry.hears: The swell's entry chord, A major (A4-C#5-E5-A5 in violins/violas/cellos), struck six times 80.67-81.47 s (v29 to v82) as the crescendo starts, the last under the violins' long Ab5: the strings' repeated chord, one attack each.

d-pedal-tolls.hears: The bass under the second half of the swell: G2 (90.7 s, 5.6 s long), C#3-D2 (99.3-100 s), then D2 restruck every ~2.2 s (100.2, 102.5, 104.6, 106.9, 108.0 s), Bb2 at 109.3 s. Slow tolls, v 55-74.

harp-bridge.hears: The bridge back to the lullaby, 110-118 s: the harp alone, one bell-like note every ~1.07 s (110.4, 111.3, 112.4, 113.5, 114.5, 115.6, 116.8 s) in harmonics F#5/F#6, D4/D6; YourMT3+ has four of the seven, the rest are the audio's onsets.

reprise-descant.hears: The lullaby returns (118.2 s) with a high, muted violin descant over it, one note per harp beat: D6-C#6-A5-Eb6-D6-Bb5-C#6-F6-Eb6-D6-C#6-A5-Eb6-D6-C#6-A5, 118.2-137 s. Soft (v 32-65), glassy, 1.1 s notes.

reprise-bassoon.hears: The bassoon's lullaby again under the descant, 123.8-135 s: D4-Bb3-C#4-C4-B3-Eb4-Bb3-D4-B3-Bb3 (bassoon track), soft and low.

lullaby-dissolve.hears: The lullaby dissolving, 154-172 s: the violins' last long notes (Ab4, Bb4, Bb5 2.5 s, Ab5, Ab5-F#5, Ab5, B4-Bb4, Bb5, Eb4) one every 1-2 s, v 30-57, over the slowing rocking.

last-rocking.hears: The last, slowest rocking notes as the Berceuse falls asleep, 172-194 s: the harp's Eb2-Bb2, Bb3 and B3/B4 and the audio's onsets between them (174.4, 182.0, 184.2, 185.5, 188.9, 191.4, 193.7 s), 1.2-7.7 s apart: farther and farther.

frozen-tremolo.hears: The spell of sleep, 194-225.2 s (-38 to -41 dB, the quietest music in the recording): the muted strings' held tremolo moving slowly from Eb minor to B major. Only its chord changes, one every 1.5-5.4 s, v 7-24: 195.05, 200.09, 204.87, 207.39, 208.91, 212.18, 217.58 s (then nothing to 225.2 s).

horn-hymn.hears: The Finale's hymn in the solo horn, 226.7-252.5 s, pianissimo over the frozen strings: F#4 (2.4 s)-E4-D#4-F#4-C#4-B3 | E4-D#4-C#4-E4-D#4-B3-C#4 (2.5 s) | F#4-E4-D#4-F#4-C#4-B3 | E4-D#4-C#4-E4-D#4. 24 notes measured in the audio (YourMT3+ has 26 short horn notes and misses the long ones).

hymn-strings.hears: The hymn's second statement, 252.4-267 s, in the strings (top line, F#4 and up): the opening chord's A4 (252.5 s), C#5, then the tune an octave above the horn, E5-D#5-F#5-C#5-B4, E5-D#5-C#5-E5-D#5-B4. Still soft (v 26-44), a little higher and fuller than the horn.

hymn-third.hears: The third statement, 267-282.8 s, louder (-23 to -20 dB): E6 over a harp sweep at 268.3 s, then E5-D#5-F#5-C#5-B4, E5-C#4-B3, C#5-E5-D#5-B4-C#5 (1.9 s). v 36-69.

hymn-crescendo.hears: The fourth statement, 282.8-303.5 s, the long crescendo (-18 to -12 dB) over the bass stepping down B2-Ab2-F#2: A5, C#5, G#5 (horn), E5-D#5-C#6, E5, Ab4, C#6-D#6 (v96 at 293.9 s)-C#6-Ab6, F#5-E5-F#5-C#6. v 48-96.

hymn-tutti.hears: The hymn fortissimo, full orchestra, 303.5-319.1 s (-7 to -4 dB, the first great arrival at 304.5 s): C#6, E6-D#6-F#6-C#6-B5-E6-F#5-E6-E5-E5-C#6-C#6, the top of the strings, 1-2 s notes, v 84-99.

hymn-entries.hears: Every entry of the hymn, one note each: the horn (226.75 s), the horn's second half (241.3 s), strings (252.48), third statement (267.0), crescendo statement (282.8), tutti (303.5), the 7/4 chords (324.13), the Maestoso (348.56 s). The theme's recurring arrival as a slow toll.

falling-bass.hears: The bass under the crescendo statements, 252-304 s: B2 (cellos, restruck and trembling 252-287 s), Ab2 (287.6 s), F#2 (291.6-303.5 s, the dominant pedal that the tutti resolves). Tremolo runs merged into held notes: a slow stepping floor, v 26-84.

keys-finale.hears: The piano track in the Finale (harp, celesta and the keyboard colour of the tutti): the B-chord arpeggio at 258.5 s, the harp sweep 268.3-269.5 s (B4-Eb5-G5-Eb6-Eb7), the rippling chords 276-284 s, the tutti chords and the Eb7 shimmer 294-303 s, the Maestoso's low F# and B chords (356.4, 370-373 s).

hush-swell.hears: The sudden hush after the tutti (319.1 s, -5 to -34 dB in 1 s) and the strings' rising crescendo out of it, 319.6-324 s: cellos trembling B2-Bb2-A2-C#3, violins climbing F5-A5-G5-Bb5 v23 -> v63, into the 7/4 chords.

seven-four-strokes.hears: The hymn recast in 7/4 (324.13-348.4 s): every note a stamping chord, one every 0.345 s, 10 bars of 7 (66 strokes detected of the 70), -10 to -3 dB; B major 324.1-333.9 s, then white-key (C/G) harmony 334.3-348.2 s. The first 3 s have no transcribed notes: these are the audio's onsets (with the roll's chord where it has one).

seven-four-downbeats.hears: The first stroke of each 7/4 bar, every 2.415 s: 324.13, 326.61, 329.00, 331.44, 333.90, 336.27, 338.66, 341.10, 343.59, 346.05 s. The bar's weight, a heavy pulse inside the stamping.

maestoso-strokes.hears: The Maestoso (348.56-381 s), the hymn in broad chords at half speed: one stroke every 0.70 s (7 to a bar), slowing to 0.8-1.0 s from 373.8 s (ritardando) into the arrival at 380.76 s. The loudest music of the piece (-5 to 0 dB); the top pitch alternates F# and B a bar or two at a time.

maestoso-downbeats.hears: The Maestoso's bar starts, every ~4.95 s: 348.56 (the F1 blow), 353.62, 358.61, 363.60, 368.64, 373.82 s, and the arrival 380.76 s. Seven huge, slow tolls.

maestoso-top.hears: The top of the Maestoso's chords from the roll (violins and the string section), one note per stroke where YourMT3+ heard it: the hymn's melody inside the stamping, 348.5-381 s, v 86-111.

maestoso-bass.hears: The bass of the 7/4 chords and the Maestoso, 324-381 s: G2 restruck under the white-key bars (336-346 s), C2 (347 s), the F1 blow (348.49 s, v110, the lowest note of the piece), then B2/F#2/E2 under the broad chords.

coda-chords.hears: The coda's slow brass chords after the arrival: B (380.76 s, ff, then held soft), B (385.65), C (387.55, restruck 388.75), Db (390.91), F (394.41), Db (396.34), C (398.55, cut at 401.1 s). 1.2-5 s apart, each held to the next: the long slow notes for a handover. Pitches from the audio's chroma (YourMT3+ has 6 notes in these 20 s).

final-chord.hears: The last chord: B major entering pianissimo at 402.40 s after a second of silence and swelling for ten seconds (-20 to -2 dB), then the final stroke at 412.62 s (-0.7 dB), cut at 413.3 s. Two long notes in four voices: the slowest, longest event of the piece.

ff-blows.hears: The real fortissimo blows, five in the whole piece: the 7/4 entry out of the hush (324.13 s), the Maestoso's first chord on the F1 (348.56), its loudest stroke (358.61, 0 dB), the arrival (380.76) and the final stroke (412.62 s). Nothing else in the recording hits like these.

melody-voiced.hears: The voiced-out line of the whole piece: of each cluster of held notes (>= 0.28 s, all tracks), the loudest; accompaniment under a louder held note left out. The melody as the ear follows it, 6.6-402 s, wherever YourMT3+ heard it (thin 172-252 s and in the 7/4 bars).

bass-line.hears: The bass of the whole piece: the lowest note below MIDI 50 of each cluster, tremolo and restruck runs merged into held notes. Soft Eb2/Bb2 in the Berceuse, D2 in its swell, B2-Ab2-F#2 under the Finale's crescendo, G2/C2/F1/B2 under the 7/4 and Maestoso.

violins-line.hears: The violin track's top line, held notes (>= 0.28 s), the whole piece: the strings' singing voice (Berceuse lament, swell and descant; the hymn from 252 s).

violas-inner.hears: The viola track's top line, held notes (>= 0.28 s): the inner voice, an octave or so under the violins (the rocking's Bb3/Ab3 early on, the swell's inner F#4/G4/Ab4, the hymn's harmony).

cellos-low.hears: The cello track's lowest line, repeats merged (gaps < 0.3 s): Eb2/Bb2 pedal, the D2 tolls, B2 tremolo, F#2 pedal, the 7/4 bass and the F1.

winds-line.hears: The wind tracks (bassoon, clarinet, horn, voice) top line, notes >= 0.2 s: the bassoon lullaby and its answers (18-60, 123-153 s), single wind touches in the swell (90-113 s), the horn notes YourMT3+ heard in the solo (228-251 s) and the clarinet-track B3/A3 at 256-274 s.

string-tremolo.hears: The string tremolo as YourMT3+ writes it: one pitch struck again and again (< 0.22 s apart, at least four in a row). The swell's repeated A chord (80.7-81.5 s), pale shimmer at 180 and 208 s (v 6-26), then the Finale's trembling build: C#5 at 254-255, B2 at 276-283, C#5/E5 at 288-289, F#2/Ab2 and the Eb7 shimmer at 297-303, the Maestoso's B5/Ab5 tremolo at 352-372 s.

fast-runs.hears: Fast stepwise runs (cluster tops < 0.22 s apart, steps of <= 4 semitones, six or more): only the violins' climb out of the hush qualifies, 319.7-323.6 s (Bb5-A5-F5-F#5-G5 ... A5, v22 to v63); the harp's sweep at 268.3 s has too few notes in the roll. YourMT3+ hears no other runs.
